definition: Child care facilities are organized settings, such as child care centers, where young children are cared for outside the home. In this context, they are places children leave and later return to, which can affect both children’s and parents’ stress and adjustment.

reasons: The definition claims child care facilities “can affect both children’s and parents’ stress and adjustment,” but the packet supports stress/distress after reopening and does not mention “adjustment.”

The definition describes child care facilities as “places children leave and later return to,” which is only specifically evidenced in the packet’s COVID-19 closure/reopening context, not as a general defining feature of child care facilities.
The claim that these settings can affect children’s and parents’ “adjustment” is not supported by the packet; the source discusses distress/stress after reopening, not adjustment as such.

The definition is slightly broader than the packet’s wording by generalizing from child care centers/center-based child care to “child care facilities” without support for that broader equivalence in the source.
